verdicts.note: Two-term incumbent first elected in 2018 [S3] and re-elected in 2022 [S4], board chair, running explicitly on 'experience matters' [S1], with a documented in-office record (public defender office [S7], annexation vote [S6]). Eight years is moderate tenure, but he is the race's proven-record case against a challenger with no record; -2 high stands, consistent with the Douglas clerk and sheriff reviews. All cited ids exist in his dossier.

S2 carries 'Limited government scope and intrusion', 'Prioritize core functions & services with a balanced budget' and 'resisting waste', which is pole_a (audit & restrain). The record items (federal money for Wenatchi Landing [S8], the grant-funded hazardous waste facility [S9], the in-house public defender [S7]) are not county-funded program expansion and do not point the other way. The evidence is his own campaign material only, so -1 medium rather than -2 or high is right. Not inferred from party.

A single campaign statement prioritizing funding for the Sheriff's office, emergency services and first responders [S2] is pole_a (police staffing); the retired-sheriff endorsement [S2] is consistent with it. The 2022 in-house public defender office [S7] concerns the quality of indigent defense, not prevention or diversion, so it is not counter-evidence. One clear statement supports medium at magnitude 1.
